title: Intel SGX Enclaves
description: Runs code in SGX enclaves isolated from the OS, hypervisor, and even physical memory attacks. The CPU encrypts enclave pages; only the enclave sees plaintext. It protects data in use from the entire software stack.

demo.title: Demo — Intel SGX Enclaves

title: AMD SEV-SNP
description: Encrypts whole VM memory with SEV-SNP so the hypervisor cannot read guest data. Integrity protection stops replay and remapping attacks that plain SEV allowed. Confidential VMs are the deployment model.

demo.title: Demo — AMD SEV-SNP

title: Intel TDX
description: Isolates trust domains with Intel TDX for VM-level confidential computing. The TDX module manages secure EPT; the host cannot inspect guest memory. It brings enclave-grade protection to whole VMs.

demo.title: Demo — Intel TDX

title: ARM TrustZone
description: Splits the processor into secure and normal worlds with TrustZone. Trusted apps run in the secure world; the normal-world OS cannot peek. Phones use it for keys and DRM.
key_mechanisms: Run TAs in the secure world

demo.title: Demo — ARM TrustZone

title: Remote Attestation
description: Proves to a remote party exactly what code runs in the enclave. The CPU signs a measurement quote; the verifier checks it against expected values. Trust becomes verifiable, not assumed.

demo.title: Demo — Remote Attestation

title: Sealing Data
description: Seals enclave data to the platform so only the same enclave on the same CPU unseals it. Sealing keys derive from the CPU and enclave identity; migrated data stays locked. It gives enclaves durable storage.

demo.title: Demo — Sealing Data

title: Enclave Paging
description: Manages the limited Enclave Page Cache with secure paging. SGX EPC is small; the driver pages encrypted enclave memory in and out. Working sets bigger than EPC pay paging costs.

demo.title: Demo — Enclave Paging

title: Side-Channel Hardening
description: Hardens enclaves against side channels: constant-time crypto, cache partitioning, branch discipline. Enclaves share hardware with attackers; the code must not leak through timing or caches. It is an ongoing arms race.

demo.title: Demo — Side-Channel Hardening

title: Memory Encryption Engines
description: Encrypts DRAM transparently with memory encryption engines like SME and MKTME. Every cache-line write encrypts; reads decrypt. It defeats cold-boot and interposer attacks with near-zero software cost.

demo.title: Demo — Memory Encryption Engines

title: Secure I/O Paths
description: Builds trusted paths from enclaves to displays and input devices. Without trusted I/O, the host can spoof what the user sees; secure paths close the gap. It is the missing link for enclave UX.

demo.title: Demo — Secure I/O Paths

title: Enclave SDKs
description: Develops with enclave SDKs that handle the enclave boundary correctly. ECALLs and OCALLs cross the boundary; the SDK marshals safely. Getting the boundary wrong leaks data.

demo.title: Demo — Enclave SDKs

title: Attestation Flows
description: Implements complete attestation flows: quote, verify, provision secrets. The relying party checks the quote then releases keys only to verified enclaves. It is how enclaves get their secrets safely.

demo.title: Demo — Attestation Flows

title: Key Provisioning
description: Provisions keys into enclaves only after successful attestation. Keys travel encrypted to the verified enclave; they never exist in host memory. It solves the enclave bootstrap problem.

demo.title: Demo — Key Provisioning

title: Enclave Debugging
description: Debugs enclaves in simulation and debug modes without weakening production. Debug enclaves allow inspection; production enclaves forbid it. The modes are cryptographically distinct.

demo.title: Demo — Enclave Debugging

title: Enclave Performance Tuning
description: Tunes enclave performance: minimize OCALLs, batch crossings, size EPC working sets. Every boundary crossing costs thousands of cycles; design keeps work inside. Measurement guides the tuning.

demo.title: Demo — Enclave Performance Tuning
